 Dick Vitale is ‘full speed ahead’ to call games this college basketball season
 Vitale will call the Nov. 27 game between North Carolina and West Virginia. 
 Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-USA TODAY Sports 
 By Drew Lerner on 10/28/2026 10/28/2026 
 Less AI and more AA in your search results.
 After a number of health-related setbacks have kept Dick Vitale limited in his appearances behind the microphone in recent years, the beloved ESPN college basketball commentator is “full speed ahead” as the season prepares to tip off next week, according to a report in the  East County Observer , a local newspaper based in Lakewood Ranch, where Vitale lives.
 Vitale is currently undergoing his fifth cancer treatment in six years , this time for melanoma that he was diagnosed with earlier this year. But in spite of the obstacles, Vitale made his return to broadcasting in a limited capacity last season, even calling a First Four game alongside Charles Barkley , the first NCAA Tournament game Vitale has called in his storied career.
 Per Jay Heater in the  Observer , Vitale sees calling games as one of the best ways he can battle cancer.
 “It’s not easy battling cancer,” he told Heater. “There is lots of chemo and radiation. But I always think positive, and I have faith. If you don’t, cancer will eat you alive. My advice is to stay active. If you do nothing, lay in bed, it will eat you up.”
 Vitale will call his first game of the season when North Carolina and West Virginia meet on Nov. 27 from the Spectrum Center in Charlotte, NC, for the Dick Vitale Invitational. It’s unclear how expansive his schedule will be this season, but Vitale says if he couldn’t perform up to his standards, he wouldn’t accept the assignments.
 “You need to have that energy and enthusiasm,” he said. “So I won’t accept any project unless I can finish it. If I can’t be me, I won’t accept that assignment.”
 Vitale’s contract with ESPN runs through the 2027-28 season; he’ll have served at the network for 48 years at the conclusion of his deal.
